venues.name: Arthurs Views
venues.signature: Five adults-only suites on Arthurs Seat ridge with panoramic Port Phillip Bay views, double spas, and electric log fires.
venues.whyWeGo: The Peninsula's most panoramic B&B position, sitting on the ridge that divides bay from hinterland, halfway between everything.

venues.name: Birch Creek
venues.signature: Two self-contained farm cottages on 40 acres near Red Hill, open fireplaces, outdoor tubs, dog-friendly, and goats.
venues.whyWeGo: Dog-friendly on 40 acres with open fires, the most genuinely rural cottage proposition in the Red Hill hinterland, at a price that makes sense.
venues.dogFriendlyNotes: Dog-friendly on 40 acres. Confirm size and breed when booking.

venues.name: Bistro Elba
venues.signature: A beachy, artfully dilapidated French bistro on Ocean Beach Road, twice-baked soufflé, ocean-trout gravlax, and a wine list built on small emerging French producers.
venues.whyWeGo: Sorrento has many restaurants that try to feel like a destination. Bistro Elba is the one that actually feels like somewhere.

venues.name: Blue Moon Cottages
venues.signature: Three 1940s cottages 250 metres from Rye bay beach, Sandpiper is the dog-friendly unit with a wood fire and fenced courtyard.
venues.whyWeGo: The clearest fireplace-and-beach cottage combination on the bayside, 1940s character, dogs welcome, and a five-minute walk to the water.
venues.dogFriendlyNotes: Sandpiper unit confirmed dog-friendly. No extra pet fee listed. Small dogs preferred. Confirm dog policy when booking.

venues.name: Brewer's Cottage — Red Hill Brewery
venues.address: 88 Shoreham Rd, Red Hill South VIC 3937
venues.signature: A three-bedroom house on the Red Hill Brewery property, stocked beer fridge, open fire, ten seconds from the bar open Thursday to Sunday.
venues.whyWeGo: You are not just sleeping near a drinks producer, you are sleeping on the producer's property, with the bar ten seconds from the front door.

venues.name: The Cape Retreat
venues.signature: Twelve luxury suites on a Cape Schanck hilltop with Bass Strait views, primarily exclusive-hire, individual suites may be available on enquiry.
venues.whyWeGo: One of the most commanding positions on the entire Peninsula, a hilltop perch with unbroken Bass Strait views that works best when the whole property is yours.

venues.name: Cassis Red Hill
venues.signature: Five adults-only villas with private heated mineral plunge pools, on the edge of Red Hill wine country with views over Western Port Bay.
venues.whyWeGo: Every villa has a private heated plunge pool on its deck, the clearest argument for Cassis over any other villa stay in the Red Hill cluster.

venues.name: Crittenden Estate
venues.signature: The Peninsula's pioneering estate, four decades of Crittenden family winemaking, Pinot, Chardonnay, and the Spanish-Italian Los Hermanos range from a new lakeside wine centre.
venues.whyWeGo: One of the founding estates of the Peninsula, now surprising visitors with Italian and Spanish varieties nobody else on the Peninsula grows.

venues.name: Crittenden Estate Villas
venues.signature: Self-contained vineyard villas on the Crittenden lake, wake up, walk to the cellar door, and eat at the on-estate restaurant without getting in a car.
venues.whyWeGo: The most complete one-location Peninsula weekend: bed, cellar door, and restaurant all on the same estate, without the managed-resort feel.

venues.name: Driftaway on Dundas
venues.signature: Three self-contained villas on 2.5 acres of tea-tree near Rye beach, breakfast hampers, oversized spa baths, one disability-accessible villa.
venues.whyWeGo: The bay-side villa option with the most complete amenity set, spa baths, breakfast hampers, and one of the few Peninsula stays with a disability-accessible unit.

venues.name: Eldridge Estate
venues.address: 120 Arthurs Seat Rd, Red Hill VIC 3937
venues.signature: David Lloyd's tiny cult estate, single-clone Pinot Noirs from individual rows, plus Gamay, made for the Burgundy obsessives.
venues.whyWeGo: Eldridge is where Peninsula Pinot nerds go to geek out, David Lloyd, a shed, a small counter, and the wines lined up for you to taste one against the other.

venues.name: Foxeys Hangout
venues.address: 795 White Hill Rd, Red Hill VIC 3937
venues.signature: Biodynamic Red Hill estate with an all-day deck, sunny long lunches, and a sparkling program that holds its own against anything French.
venues.whyWeGo: Foxeys is one of the Peninsula's most consistently pleasant cellar doors, sunny, unpretentious, and serious about the wine without making you work for it.

venues.name: Georgie Bass Cafe & Cookery
venues.signature: All-day cafe on Cook Street built around produce from their own farm, the natural anchor for a Flinders morning or a post-cliff-walk lunch.
venues.whyWeGo: All-day breakfast until 3pm, own-farm produce, a cookery school on-site, the best reason to base a Flinders visit around lunch rather than dinner.

venues.name: Happy Glamper
venues.signature: Mobile bell-tent glamping that pitches styled tents at nominated Peninsula foreshore campsites, setup and packdown handled, children welcome.
venues.whyWeGo: The most flexible glamping format on the Peninsula, they pitch, style, and pack down; you arrive to a ready tent at your chosen foreshore site.

venues.name: Hideaways at Red Hill
venues.signature: Spa cottages for two with gas fires and in-room spa baths, walking distance from Red Hill village and the weekend market.
venues.whyWeGo: The hinterland wine-country cottage position at a price below the estate villas, spa bath, gas fire, and the Saturday market on foot.

venues.name: Hurley Vineyard
venues.signature: Kevin Bell's boutique single-vineyard Pinot project, three tiny blocks (Lodestone, Garamond, Hommage) and some of the Peninsula's most sought-after bottles.
venues.whyWeGo: The cellar door where the wines are already sold out and the conversation with Kevin is the product.

venues.name: Iluka Retreat & Camp
venues.signature: Thirty structures on 36 acres near Shoreham, the Peninsula's only fixed-site multi-tent group glamping venue, with a private freshwater lake.
venues.whyWeGo: The Peninsula's only fixed-site glamping venue built for groups, the right answer for retreats and social weekends that need real outdoor infrastructure.

venues.name: Mornington Peninsula Retro Caravans
venues.signature: Restored 1950s–60s themed caravans 500 metres from Rye bay beach, dog-friendly in designated units, the most characterful glamping-adjacent option on the bayside.
venues.whyWeGo: Retro caravans, 500 metres from the bay beach, dogs welcome, the most accessible and characterful overnight option on the bay side.
venues.dogFriendlyNotes: Dogs welcome in designated units at $22/night fee. Confirm breed and size when booking.

venues.name: Kooyong
venues.address: 263 Red Hill Rd, Red Hill South VIC 3937
venues.signature: Single-vineyard pinot noir and chardonnay from one of the Peninsula's most decorated estates.
venues.whyWeGo: The single-block tasting is a practical education in why micro-terroir matters, side-by-side pinot noirs from adjacent slopes that actually taste different from each other.

venues.name: Main Ridge Estate
venues.signature: Planted in 1975 by Nat and Rosalie White, the Peninsula's founding vineyard, still making restrained Pinot and Chardonnay from the original blocks.
venues.whyWeGo: Main Ridge Estate is the vineyard that started it all, planted in 1975 when nobody in Victoria quite believed cool-climate Pinot could be taken seriously.

venues.name: Mantons Creek Estate
venues.signature: Four adults-only vineyard suites with on-estate Italian dining, two minutes from Ten Minutes by Tractor, the most under-indexed southern Red Hill base.
venues.whyWeGo: The only southern Red Hill stay where the on-estate restaurant removes the need to choose between dinner and a second glass of wine.
knownFor: Southern Red Hill Winery Circuit Access

venues.name: Merricks General Wine Store
venues.signature: The old Merricks general store reborn as a cellar door, bakery, and produce-forward lunch room.
venues.whyWeGo: The room that makes the Peninsula feel like it still belongs to itself, unhurried, unfussy, and entirely of where it is.

venues.name: Montalto Vineyard & Olive Grove
venues.address: 33 Shoreham Rd, Red Hill South VIC 3937
venues.signature: Single Vineyard Pinot Noir and a Sunday lunch beneath the olive grove canopy.
venues.whyWeGo: The Peninsula's most complete estate experience, sculpture, garden, cellar door, and a one-hat kitchen, done at a scale that still feels human rather than corporate.

venues.name: Moorooduc Estate
venues.signature: Richard McIntyre's pioneering low-intervention estate, home to the Robinson Chardonnay, one of Australia's genuine Chardonnay reference points.
venues.whyWeGo: The Robinson Chardonnay is one of the benchmarks for what the variety can be in this country, and McIntyre has been here since before most of the Peninsula's celebrated producers planted their first vines.

venues.name: Mornington Main Street Market
venues.signature: The northern Peninsula's midweek town market, a broad mix that folds easily into a Mornington visit.

venues.name: Mount Eliza Farmers Market
venues.address: Mount Eliza Village, Mt Eliza VIC 3930
venues.signature: A smaller community farmers market in Mount Eliza village, producers drawn from the Mornington corridor.

venues.name: Mornington Peninsula Beach Club Cottages
venues.signature: Five two-bedroom bay-beach cottages in Tootgarook, EV charging, disability access, private yards, and eight minutes from Peninsula Hot Springs.
venues.whyWeGo: Bay beach, EV charging, disability access, the most practically equipped family and accessibility-friendly cottage option on the bayside.
venues.dogFriendlyNotes: Pet-friendly with private yards. Confirm breed, size, and unattended-dog policy before booking.

venues.name: Ocean Eight Vineyard
venues.signature: Mike Aylward's precise, minimal cellar door turning out some of the Peninsula's most quietly obsessive pinot noir.
venues.whyWeGo: Mike Aylward grew up in Peninsula wine, his family founded Kooyong, and Ocean Eight is what he built when he decided smaller and more single-minded was the right call.

venues.name: Paradigm Hill
venues.signature: George Mihaly's fastidiously farmed single-site Pinot Noir estate, appointment-only tastings, often led by George himself.
venues.whyWeGo: One of the very few Peninsula estates where the founder is routinely in the room, pouring and talking, on a Saturday afternoon.

venues.name: Paringa Estate
venues.address: 44 Paringa Rd, Red Hill South VIC 3937
venues.signature: A serious single-vineyard producer with one of the Peninsula's most dependable restaurant terraces.
venues.whyWeGo: Lindsay McCall's pinot noir and shiraz have been Peninsula benchmarks for decades, the cellar door and terrace restaurant are where you taste that track record without ceremony.

venues.name: Peninsula Hot Springs Eco Lodges
venues.signature: Fully enclosed eco lodges inside the Peninsula Hot Springs precinct, private in-room geothermal baths and the same 5am access as the glamping tents.
venues.whyWeGo: The enclosed upgrade over PHS Glamping, private geothermal water in your room or on your deck, and no shared amenities block between you and the thermal pools.

venues.name: Plantation House at Whitecliffs
venues.signature: Heritage 1932 sandstone property 150 metres from Rye's front beach, host Charles's cooked breakfasts are named in almost every recent review.
venues.whyWeGo: 150 metres from the front beach, a 9.7 Booking.com score, and a host whose breakfasts have become a structural feature of the stay, not a variable.

venues.name: Point Nepean Discovery Tents
venues.address: Point Nepean National Park, Portsea VIC 3944
venues.signature: Forty-six pre-pitched canvas tents inside Point Nepean National Park, September to April, from $115 a night, inside the historic quarantine station precinct.
venues.whyWeGo: The Peninsula's most atmospheric glamping setting, sleeping inside a national park quarantine station at the southernmost tip, under $130 a night for two.

venues.name: Polperro
venues.address: 150 Red Hill Rd, Red Hill South VIC 3937
venues.signature: Small-production cool-climate pinot and chardonnay poured in one of the prettiest tasting rooms on the ridge.
venues.whyWeGo: Polperro's scale, small, owner-operated, unhurried, is the thing itself, not just a selling point; the room rewards the kind of afternoon you don't try to plan.

venues.name: Port Phillip Estate
venues.address: 263 Red Hill Rd, Red Hill South VIC 3937
venues.signature: Rammed-earth architecture, a one-hat restaurant, and six hotel suites set into the pinot rows of Main Ridge.
venues.whyWeGo: The Peninsula's most architecturally serious winery stay, where the building, the wine, and the room are all working at the same level.

venues.name: Pt. Leo Estate
venues.signature: A sculpture park walk followed by a long bay-view lunch in the glass-walled restaurant.
venues.whyWeGo: Ninety-three hectares where the sculpture and the wine and the bay view arrive simultaneously, no other Peninsula property asks this much of its setting and delivers on all three counts.

venues.name: Quealy Winemakers
venues.signature: A foundational Peninsula producer best known for pinot gris, friulano, and a cellar door with real local soul.
venues.whyWeGo: Quealy helped teach the Peninsula what it could grow beyond pinot and chardonnay, the cellar door still carries that experimental, unpretentious spirit.

venues.name: Red Hill Cheese
venues.signature: Small-batch cheesemaker with a tasting room, hard sheep's milk styles, washed rinds, and a rotating seasonal list.
venues.whyWeGo: Red Hill Cheese is one of the Peninsula's quietest food landmarks, the tasting room where the cheesemaker talks through milk sourcing, ageing, and why Peninsula terroir matters in the fromagerie.

venues.name: Red Hill Estate
venues.signature: One of the Peninsula's most photographed cellar-door positions, sweeping Western Port views and a serious traditional-method sparkling program.
venues.whyWeGo: The view from the tasting room, vineyard slope dropping to Western Port, French Island in the middle distance, is the most dramatic cellar-door position on the plateau.

venues.name: Rye Beachside Market
venues.address: Rye Foreshore, Point Nepean Rd, Rye VIC 3941
venues.signature: A Sunday-morning stall row on the Rye foreshore, with the bay a few metres away.

venues.name: The Sanctuary at Alba
venues.signature: Five standalone villas on the Alba Thermal Springs estate, the Peninsula's first overnight stay with all-day thermal access built in.
venues.whyWeGo: The Sanctuary solves what no Peninsula hot-springs property has before: the thermal bathing is not a day-trip you attach to the stay, it is what the stay is built around.

venues.name: Sorrento Gelato
venues.signature: The Ocean Beach Road gelato window, classic Italian flavours, a rotating seasonal list, and a compulsory stop on any summer evening stroll.
venues.whyWeGo: Sorrento Gelato is the window on Ocean Beach Road that everybody in Sorrento joins the queue for at least once per visit, and once is never enough.

venues.name: Sourdough Kitchen
venues.signature: A small-batch sourdough baker at the top of Mornington's Main Street, long-fermented loaves, a tight pastry line, and the best bread in town.
venues.whyWeGo: The Mornington baker that wine-room people quietly recommend when someone asks where the best bread is, bread-first, small room, loyal locals.

venues.name: Stonier Wines
venues.signature: One of the Peninsula's founding estates, planted in 1978, grown-up, unflashy, with some of the oldest Chardonnay vines in the region.
venues.whyWeGo: When you want a cellar door built around the wine rather than the experience around the wine, Stonier is the answer on the Peninsula.
knownFor: Planted 1978 by Brian and Noel Stonier, one of the Peninsula's founding estates
Reserve Chardonnay and KBS Vineyard Pinot Noir as benchmark wines
Among the oldest Chardonnay vines in the region
No wedding marquee, no sculpture trail, purely a wine operation

venues.name: T'Gallant
venues.signature: The Peninsula's Pinot Grigio pioneer, a family-friendly cellar door on Main Ridge with Italian-inspired food and the estate's Prosecco by the glass.
venues.whyWeGo: Not every cellar door visit needs to be a serious wine occasion. T'Gallant is where you go when the table is mixed, the afternoon is loose, and you want food that keeps up with the wine.
knownFor: Planted by Kathleen Quealy and Kevin McCarthy in the late 1980s, the Peninsula's Pinot Grigio pioneers
First estate to establish Pinot Grigio as a serious Peninsula variety
Most reliably family-friendly cellar door on Main Ridge
Italian-inspired food menu with shaded outdoor seating
Open daily, one of few cellar doors that doesn't require planning

venues.name: Ten Minutes by Tractor
venues.signature: Estate-grown pinot noir alongside a seasonal degustation rooted in the Ridge vineyard.
venues.whyWeGo: Two hats and the most considered wine program on the Peninsula, a degustation that tastes like the specific slope outside the window, not just the region.

venues.name: The Orchard Luxury Accommodation
venues.signature: Three rammed-earth self-contained apartments on ten acres of Red Hill South wine country, in-room spa baths, infrared sauna, and valley views.
venues.whyWeGo: The rammed-earth architecture and the in-room spa baths put this well above most $$ cottage options in the hinterland, and the host is a phone call away, not a chatbot.
knownFor: Three self-contained rammed-earth apartments on ten acres in Red Hill South wine country
In-room spa baths and infrared sauna, both uncommon at this price point
Lake and valley views from all units
Small dogs welcome with a $50 additional fee
Host Frank Haddy's direct mobile on the website, a genuinely reachable host
venues.dogFriendlyNotes: Small dogs welcome at a $50 fee. Confirm size and breed when booking.

venues.name: Treetops at Red Hill
venues.address: 80 McIlroys Rd, Red Hill South VIC 3937
venues.signature: Two quiet self-contained cottages opposite a micro-vineyard, local breakfast provisions included, and Port Phillip Estate under a kilometre away.
venues.whyWeGo: Proximity to Port Phillip Estate alone makes this address worth knowing. The included breakfast provisions and the micro-vineyard view are a bonus at a price point where most options make you work harder for less.
knownFor: Two self-contained cottages directly opposite a micro-vineyard on McIlroys Road
Local breakfast provisions included and stocked in the fridge on arrival
Port Phillip Estate 0.9km away, the Peninsula's highest-rated winery within walking distance
A new entrant to the market, one of the freshest wine-adjacent stay options in Red Hill
Genuinely affordable base for a cellar-door weekend

venues.name: Villa Mallorca
venues.signature: Two suites in a Majorcan finca-style property in Mt Martha, where the hosts are named in 212 TripAdvisor reviews and are the actual product.
venues.whyWeGo: Paul plays Spanish guitar on the terrace on no fixed schedule, Sheree delivers home-cooked food to the door unannounced, neither is available as an add-on at a managed hotel.

venues.name: Willow Creek Vineyard
venues.signature: The vineyard at the heart of Jackalope Hotel, a showpiece single-site program and the home of both Rare Hare and Doot Doot Doot.
venues.whyWeGo: Willow Creek is the one Peninsula vineyard where the winemaking, the cellar door, and the two-hat restaurant are all drawing from the same block of vines, the coherence between them is the point.

venues.name: Woodman Estate
venues.signature: Three lakeside chalets over a private five-acre lake on a 50-acre English country estate, the Peninsula's most pastoral villa option.
venues.whyWeGo: The only Peninsula villa where the water is directly underneath you, three private chalets built over a five-acre lake, closer to the English country-house tradition than anything else in the region.

venues.name: Yabby Lake Vineyard
venues.signature: Tom Carson's single-block Chardonnay and Pinot Noir program, poured from a relaxed cellar door with one of the Peninsula's loveliest lunch decks.
venues.whyWeGo: The Block 1 Pinot was the first Pinot to ever win the Jimmy Watson Trophy, the cellar door is the right place to understand why, and the deck is reason enough to stay.

venues.name: Yurt Hideaway
venues.signature: A traditional 6-metre Mongolian yurt in Tootgarook, five minutes from Peninsula Hot Springs, hosted by yoga instructors, 4.97 stars.
venues.whyWeGo: The rating is the first indicator. The hosting philosophy, yoga instructors who designed a space for disconnection, not content, is the second. Five minutes from Peninsula Hot Springs is the third.
knownFor: A traditional 6-metre Mongolian yurt in Tootgarook, the only one of its kind on the Peninsula
4.97-star Airbnb rating across a 100% recommendation rate
Hosted by yoga instructors, designed intentionally for rest and disconnection
Five minutes from Peninsula Hot Springs
Private fenced courtyard, separate en-suite, outdoor kitchenette
